units.text: INT. FUNICULAR CAR - MIDNIGHT
A small wooden car climbs a steep rail above a sleeping alpine town.
A single lamp swings from the roof.
Below, the lights of the Hotel Edelweiss glitter.
VESPER KOWALCZYK, 40s, elegant, in a conductor's cap and uniform that almost fits, stands at the brake wheel.
She is the picture of calm.
LORENZO, 30s, bellhop's jacket, crouches on a long steamer trunk.
ODILE, 50s, in a fur coat that does not belong to her, sits upright on the bench with a cane across her knees.
HIRO, 20s, thin, quiet, wearing a night porter's apron, holds a canvas tool roll.
Four minutes to the top station. We stop at the second landing for the cable.
units.name: VESPER

units.text: The cable is on the trunk?
units.name: LORENZO

units.text: The cable is the trunk.
units.name: VESPER

units.text: Odile taps her cane twice on the floor.
Hiro unrolls his tools without a sound.
What does the guard say when the car stops?
units.name: LORENZO

units.text: The guard has been drinking since nine.
units.name: ODILE

units.text: The guard is a gentleman. He sleeps well.
units.name: VESPER

units.text: The car shudders over a joint in the rail.
Everyone grips something.
Then it settles, and the hum of the cable resumes.
There is a second car coming down.
units.name: HIRO

units.text: They look.
Through the rear window, a pair of lights, small, then larger, sliding down the opposite track.
That's the midnight milk run. It passes us at the landing.
units.name: VESPER

units.text: Nobody said there was a milk run.
units.name: LORENZO

units.text: Nobody checked the timetable but me.
units.name: VESPER

units.text: The oncoming car rumbles past, inches off.
Its single passenger, a man in a doorman's coat, looks through the glass.
He sees the trunk.
He sees four conductors.
His mouth opens.
Vesper tips her cap.
The man blinks, tips his own, and sinks out of view.
He will remember that.
units.name: ODILE

units.text: He will remember a nice woman in a nice cap.
units.name: VESPER

units.text: The car clanks to a halt at the second landing.
Silence.
A lantern glows on a platform ahead, and a figure steps into it: the GUARD, an enormous man, fully awake, holding a rifle.
Good evening, Frau Kowalczyk.
units.name: GUARD

units.text: Nobody moves.
Lorenzo's hand drifts toward the trunk.
Odile's cane rises an inch.
Hiro's wrench disappears into his sleeve.
Good evening, Anselm. You are not drunk.
units.name: VESPER

units.text: Not tonight. Tonight I was told.
units.name: GUARD

units.text: Vesper closes her eyes briefly, then opens them.
Hiro. Now.
units.name: VESPER

units.text: Hiro slams the brake lever.
The car bucks.
The trunk slides, Lorenzo with it, and both crash into the Guard's legs.
The rifle goes off into the roof.
Odile lashes the cane across his wrist.
He roars and swings.
Vesper hauls the trunk's lid open.
Cable spills out in a silver snake.
Hiro and Lorenzo wrestle the Guard onto the platform.
Odile steps over them in her borrowed fur.
Vesper takes the lantern from the rail and casts it away into the dark.
It falls and falls and falls.
We have two minutes before the top station knows.
units.name: ODILE

units.text: We have one. Everybody in the car.
units.name: VESPER

units.text: They scramble in.
The car lurches uphill, faster, and the lights of the Edelweiss rush up to meet them.
